note: Weight vectors over spec/endpoints.json. A blend either writes its vector out or derives one: 'derive' takes the 'comparable' field off each family in spec/endpoints.json and zeroes every endpoint whose family does not say the named thing, so the reason a row is excluded lives where the endpoint is defined and adding a family cannot quietly add it to a ranking. The request stream is drawn uniformly, so every opinion about traffic lives here and nowhere else. A vector need not sum to anything: weights are relative and normalised when the blend is composed. Weights are applied by scaling each endpoint's histogram before merging, and percentiles are read from the merged histogram; a blend is never an average of per-endpoint percentiles. Adding a blend needs no re-measurement, only a re-run of harness/summarize.py over samples already on disk.

uniform.title: Uniform
uniform.why: The published headline. Every endpoint counts once, so the number carries no opinion about traffic. It is also the only blend with no reweighting error, because a uniform mix is the mix that was actually run: per-endpoint latency is not independent of the mix, so every other vector here describes what those endpoints did under uniform load rather than under their own.

rankable.title: Rankable
rankable.why: Uniform with every family that is not comparable across frameworks removed. Template output is partly an engine benchmark, so a ranking that includes it measures Thymeleaf against html/template; a response cache is partly a store benchmark, and several targets run a package chosen for them rather than one the framework ships.

core.title: Core
core.why: What blend-v1 covered: dispatch, serialization, routing, body handling, query parsing, application work and errors, with every feature family zeroed. The old series has no successor that carries its numbers, but this one carries its shape.

features.title: Features
features.why: Only what a real service turns on. Separates frameworks that are quick at dispatch from frameworks that are quick once authorization, compression, caching and a middleware chain are in the path.

read-only.title: Read only
read-only.why: A service behind a cache, where reads dominate and the write path barely runs. Every endpoint carrying a request body is zeroed, which drops validation and the four write methods.
